blind.why: B Site from B Door (-24,0,-38) vs CS2 Italy market. The ref has one strong focal cover piece (a pergola stall with string lights), real sun/shade contrast and a clear ground plane. Ours is cohesive but flat: a crate fills the camera, there are more crates and a plinth, the plaza has no focal cover, and lighting is even with soft, weak shadows.

Upper Tunnel (-33,0,-6) vs CS2 sunlit arches. Ours is lit like an office corridor: the cream tiled ceiling glows as bright as the outdoor site, so the tunnel has no sense of darkness and the exit has no light pull. The ref uses hard light and shadow to shape the space and lead the eye.

Long seen from Long Ramp (38,1.5,-12) vs CS2 Banana alley. Ours is a 60 m beige canyon: two identical teal containers, repeated small windows and bunting, no framing and no mid-ground layering. The ref frames the lane with an arch, lights, a barrel pile and layered depth.

biggest_gap: Lighting has no value hierarchy, so interiors and exteriors read the same. All tunnels (Tunnel Approach (-26,0,43), Lower (-34,0,0), Upper (-33,0,-6)), the Mid Doors arch and B Connector are lit almost as brightly as the open sites. The cream ceiling tiles glow, so the tunnels feel like a bright hallway, and the lamps change only the tint (orange, cyan, amber), not the value. Outdoors, sun shadows are soft and low-contrast and the image has a milky haze (Long, A site, Tide Spawn). Reproduce with ?test=1&seed=1&scene=map-overview and a camera at (-33,1.64,-6) looking toward (-33,0,-26). CS2 makes interiors and covered lanes about 2 to 3 stops darker than the sunlit exits, so a player stands out against the exit (Dust2 tunnels, Inferno Banana, Mirage connector), and uses hard sun shadows for depth. Darken roofed volumes with a per-zone ambient/AO multiplier of about 0.4 to 0.5 and use darker ceiling materials, keep pools of lamp light, and harden and darken the sun shadows outdoors.
other_gaps: The tunnel bends do not differ in identity at eye height. Lower (-34,0,0) and Upper (-33,0,-6) both read as cream plaster, teal wainscot and brick arches with a pendant lamp; only the Tunnel Approach floor is distinctively terracotta. A screenshot does not tell you which bend you are in.

Cover is generic and evenly spread. Sites are made of the same building blocks: 1 m sandstone blocks, crates, containers, a lone pillar (A at (31,1.5,-30): a block plus crate rows; Hub: a pillar plus low blocks). There is no signature cover piece per site (a pergola, cart, car, well or stall) that players would name and play around. B Site is a market square with a parasol and a crate rather than a defended site.

Long (38,0,-12 to 36) is a monotone beige canyon: two identical teal containers, the same window and bunting rhythm on both sides, and nothing that frames the 60 m sightline. Add an arch or overpass, varied facade depth and a pile of mid-lane props.

Mid Lane is a dead-straight 30 m corridor from the Ember Spawn floor (0,46) to the Mid Doors arch. It reads well, but there is no bend or break, so spawn peeks down Mid are guaranteed. Spawn-to-spawn LOS is still 3 of 9216 pairs, longest 99 m, from (-3,49) to (9,-49).

There is no fast Tide rotation through the centre. rotate-a-to-b-palace is 109 m and takes 15.0 s in the real sim, because A has to go north through the Catwalk to the Hub and then back south. The through-spawn route takes 10 s. Palace, the map's central landmark, is not a rotation connector.

Clouds are chains of overlapping white ellipsoids that look like caterpillars (A Site looking west, c_a_to_catwalk) and look cheap against an otherwise clean sky. The literal KIOSK sign in Tide Mid (0,0,-33) reads as a placeholder.
B Connector entrance (-14,0,-21): two dark palm trunks stand in the doorway and clutter the chokepoint silhouette.
bugs: Callout mismatch: at (0,0,-36) calloutAt returns 'Tide Spawn' while the floor decal 2 m ahead reads 'TIDE MID'.
heightAt(44,30) and heightAt(-8,-30) return rooftop height 8.5, not the walkable floor, which is risky for any consumer that places things on the floor.
strengths: Real movement-sim traversal at 7.2 m/s: all 9 PATHS complete with zero stalls. Ember reaches A in 10.9 s (Long) or 12.1 s (Short) and B in 12.0 s (Mid) or 11.6 s (Tunnels); Tide reaches A or B in 4.6 s; the A to B rotation through spawn takes 10 s.
Wall-slide scan: 700 samples, median 6.7 m/s along walls. The only stops were in unreachable prop pockets, so I found no real collision snags.
Cohesive, readable stylised palette. Team-tinted spawns, A teal and B terracotta site floors, floor callout decals and signage (MID DOORS, B CONNECTOR) make orientation easy.
Landmarks are now distinct: the teal-domed A tower, the clock tower, the minaret and the water tower are visible over the roofline.
Perf: 66 to 75 draw calls and about 140k triangles for the whole map, with 0 console errors.
